security_spec.violation_condition: When the XiangShan integer execution unit implements signed averaging add instructions (PAADD.B, PAADD.H, PAADD.W, AADD, PAADD.DB, PAADD.DH, PAADD.DW) but uses logical right shift (zero-fill, >>_logical) instead of arithmetic right shift (sign-extending, >>_arith) on the intermediate sum, the result for negative operands rounds toward zero instead of toward negative infinity as mandated by the spec. For example, signed(-3) + signed(0) = -3, then logical shift (-3)>>1 produces 0x7E (126 unsigned, or -1 if interpreted as signed, which is truncation toward zero) instead of the correct 0xFF (-1 via arithmetic shift, which is floor toward negative infinity). Similarly, if the add intermediate sum is computed at insufficient precision (e.g., 8 bits for byte elements instead of 9 bits, 16 bits for halfword instead of 17 bits, or 32 bits for word instead of 33 bits), the carry bit is lost before the shift, corrupting the averaged result.
security_spec.summary: Signed averaging add must use arithmetic right shift (sign-extending) and full (N+1)-bit intermediate sum to implement round-toward-negative-infinity; using logical shift or narrow adders silently corrupts negative results
